summary: Contestants demonstrate their knowledge of personal finance by analyzing topics such as credit, taxes, investments, insurance, and retirement strategies. Participants solve real-world scenarios using financial calculations and risk management concepts.
time_limits: no more than ten (10) minutes for orientation
no more than sixty (60) minutes for testing
no more than ten (10) minutes for wrap-up
what_to_bring: Published and/or unpublished non-electronic written reference materials
Cordless calculator: Electronic devices will be monitored according to ACT standards. See NLC Calculator Guidelines. Contestants who violate this rule will be disqualified.
competencies: Explain the functions of key regulatory agencies in overseeing financial institutions and protecting consumers, emphasizing compliance and ethical standards
Analyze credit agreements, costs, and regulatory protections to make informed borrowing decisions
Describe common identity theft tactics and recommend proactive measures for safeguarding personal data
Apply mathematical methods to calculate simple and compound interest, supporting accurate financial planning and cost analysis
Interpret personal income tax concepts, including deductions, credits, and filing requirements, to support compliance and financial planning
Describe the role of credit bureaus and analyze factors influencing credit scores
Evaluate the financial and legal consequences of bankruptcy, including costs, long-term impacts, and alternatives
Compare features, benefits, and tax implications of retirement plans and assess strategies for different life stages to promote lifelong financial security
Identify and explain major types of insurance, distinguish insurable vs. self-insurable risks, analyze factors affecting premiums, and calculate benefits to support effective risk management

Analyze investment options by evaluating risk, return, liquidity, and diversification, calculating and comparing rates of return, and explaining how diversification reduces risk and supports optimized returns
Differentiate between preferred and common stock, calculate dividends based on company policies, and interpret factors influencing stock price movements to apply basic analysis for predicting trends
Compare mutual fund categories and evaluate their suitability for different investment goals
Distinguish between corporate and government bonds, analyzing features, risks, and returns
eligibility_notes: Any secondary or postsecondary division contestant may enter this application event.
